1.explanation:
• packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.js & index.js – This is where the <Tabs> component is defined and exported. It needs to accept a new `size` prop (e.g. "default" | "large") and propagate it to its TabList/Tab children.
• packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.mdx & Tabs-story.js – The documentation and story for Tabs must be updated to document the new `size` prop and show the 48px large variant.
• packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs-test.js & tabs-test.e2e.js – Unit and E2E tests currently assume only a 40px tab. They need new assertions for the large 48px size and for the correct icon offset.
• packages/react/src/components/Tab/Tab.js – The Tab component handles the individual tab rendering and class names. It must apply a modifier class (e.g. `--icon-only--large`) or inline style based on the `size` prop so that its width/height and icon positioning update.
• styles/scss/components/tabs/_tabs.scss – The core styles for the tabs variants live here. You need to define the CSS for the large icon-only size (48px dimensions and 20px inner offset) under a new modifier, and ensure the default 40px rules remain intact.
1.bug_scenario: The icon-only variant of the Tabs component currently has no built-in support for two distinct sizes: it’s always hard-coded (or manually styled) as 40×40, and there’s no `size` prop to toggle a larger 48×48 option. The bug report and screenshot show that both the Line (default) and ContainedTabs variants need to be able to render at 40px (default) or 48px (large) when an icon-only tab is used, and the offset of the icon inside the tab boundary must also adjust (16px vs 20px).

2.explanation:
• packages/components/src/components/tabs/tabs.config.js & tabs.js
  – This is the vanilla Web Components configuration and implementation of the Tabs API. We must add and document the new `size` prop at the lowest level so that it’s available in all consumers (vanilla, React, etc.).

• packages/carbon-react/scss/components/tabs/_tabs.scss
  – The SCSS for Tabs defines icon-only dimensions. We need to introduce a modifier class (e.g. `--icon-only--large`) that sets the width/height to 48 px and adjusts vertical alignment (20 px), while preserving the existing 40 px default.

• react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.js & react/src/components/Tabs/next/Tabs.js
  – The React wrapper components must accept the new `size` prop, default it to “default”, and apply the corresponding CSS modifier to the rendered markup.

• react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs-test.js
  – Update or add unit tests to cover both default and large icon-only variants, asserting correct class names and computed dimensions.

• react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.stories.js
  – Update the Storybook stories to expose the new `size` control and demonstrate both 40 px and 48 px variants for icon-only Tabs.

• react/src/components/Tab/Tab.js
  – The individual Tab item needs to consume the `size` context (or prop) in order to apply the correct padding/positioning classes for the icon-only state.  

Together, these changes ensure that the new `size` prop is fully wired through from configuration and styling up into the React component API, stories, and tests.
2.bug_scenario: The icon-only Tabs variant (both Line and ContainedTabs) currently only renders with a 40 px tappable area and icon centering. The design calls for two sizes: default (40 px) and "large" (48 px), with the icon vertically offset by 16 px or 20 px respectively. Users must be able to pass a new `size` prop ("default" | "large") to the Tabs component to switch between those dimensions.
